regime: Risk-On Reclaim / Post-CPI (NQ, ES, gold flip back long)
summary: Cool CPI, risk back on. July inflation landed in line with forecasts and a touch softer year over year, and the market treated it as the all-clear it had been de-risking for. NQ gapped up overnight, tagged 30,001.5 above the 30,000 psych level, and though it faded through the day it still closed 29,807.25 (+0.54%), back above the trend stop it lost on Tuesday. The S&P did the same, reclaiming its stop and closing green at 7,766.5 (+0.17%). Gold repaired Tuesday's crack, closing 4,435.7 (+0.93%) back above its stop. The clearest tell was fear coming out of the market: the VIX collapsed to 14.55, down 4.78%, and spot gold and silver both firmed. Crude was the lone holdout, down 0.78% to 82.59, still under its stop and now losing its average. So three of four symbols repaired their Tuesday short flips, but note the shape of the day: this was a gap up that faded, not a trend that ran. The relief buying came overnight and the RTH sold the highs.
psychology: The lesson today is about the head-fake, and about not chasing the gap. We told you Tuesday that the first move after an 8:30 print is often not the real one, and today showed both sides of it. The benign number sent everything higher overnight, and if you bought that gap at the highs, you spent the whole RTH session watching it bleed back. NQ gave back more than a hundred points off its 29,946 high into the close. That is the trap of an event day: the emotional move is up front, and the market spends the rest of the session sorting out what the number actually means. The professionals did not chase the open. They let the relief spike happen, waited to see whether price could accept above a level with two hourly closes, and most of it could not hold the highs. Reclaiming a stop and closing near your session low, like NQ did, is a weaker signal than reclaiming and closing strong. It counts, but it is a soft reclaim. Respect the difference. And with PPI on Thursday, the same discipline carries: carry less into the print, trade the reaction, not the anticipation.

event.name: July CPI comes in cool, risk-on reclaim
event.consensus: Headline CPI was expected near +0.1% on the month and 3.4% year over year, with core near +0.2% and 2.5%. All four readings matched the Wall Street consensus tracked by Dow Jones and FactSet.
event.actual: The July CPI report landed at 8:30 AM ET and it was benign. Headline prices rose 0.1% on the month for a 3.4% annual rate, cooler than June, and core prices (excluding food and energy) rose 0.2% for a 2.5% annual rate, also a step down. Both the headline and the core matched consensus, and the core continued its slow multi-month cooling.
event.surprise: There was no upside surprise to punish the market, and after two sessions of de-risking into the number, that was enough to trigger a relief rally. The VIX collapsed 4.78% to 14.55 as event risk cleared.
event.nqReaction: The reaction was textbook risk-on. Equities gapped up overnight. NQ ran to 30,001.5, just above the 30,000 psych level, then spent the RTH giving it back, closing 29,807.25 (+0.54%) but back above the trend stop it lost Tuesday.
event.crossAsset: ES reclaimed its stop and closed green at 7,766.5 (+0.17%). Gold repaired its Tuesday crack, closing 4,435.7 (+0.93%) with spot gold (4,408.21, +0.88%) and silver both firm. Crude was the exception, sliding 0.78% to 82.59 and staying under its stop. The important nuance: the buying was an overnight relief spike, and the RTH faded it. This was a repair of the short flips, not a fresh trend day, and it comes with PPI still to clear on Thursday.

risk.ddProximity: REDUCED band, still leaning careful into PPI
risk.sizing: Realized volatility fell further today, with NQ's ATR down to 75.38 and the VIX at 14.55, so risk per contract is contained and the tape is calm. The read improved: three of four symbols reclaimed their trend stops, so the board is no longer uniformly defensive. But two things keep the throttle down. First, the reclaims are soft, one day old, and the equities closed near their session lows after fading a relief gap, which is a weak-handed repair rather than a fresh trend. Second, there is another 8:30 ET print on Thursday with PPI.
risk.openRisk: When a repair is fragile and another catalyst is one session away, the honest move is the same as yesterday: carry less, not more. PPI can reprice every level on this page in seconds. Let it land, wait for acceptance beyond a level (two hourly closes, not a knee-jerk spike), and trade the reaction rather than the anticipation.
risk.dailyLossBudget: Trim size as PPI approaches; do not carry full risk into the print.
risk.note: Thursday's July PPI at 8:30 AM ET is the next event, with retail sales and University of Michigan sentiment Friday. Plan exposure into PPI, respect your prop-firm blackout rules, and remember the first move after the print is often not the real one, which is exactly what today's gap-and-fade just showed.

Three of the four opening ranges broke DOWN first (NQ, ES, and crude), and only gold broke up. That is the fade tell: the market gapped up on the print, then sellers took the RTH the other way. NQ's opening range topped right at the 30,001.5 overnight high, a failed poke above the 30,000 psych level, and the down-break at 15:00 UTC ran price all the way to the 29,807 close. The session NYVWAP for NQ sat at 29,886, and price closed below it, another sign the RTH belonged to the sellers even on a green day.

HTA OPEN eligibility Thursday: Thursday is not Monday, not Wednesday, not FOMC, and PPI is not a filtered event, so all four plays (BIR, HOF, MID, BNC) are eligible. An 8:30 PPI open is still high-variance, so treat eligibility as a rules green light, not a push to trade. Eligibility note, not a trade instruction.

MNQ reclaims the 29,795 stop on 2 hourly closes after the printTRIGGEREDPLAYED OUTNQ reclaimed 29,795 on the gap and closed above it every RTH hour. The short flip was neutralized and it repaired past the 29,887 target the row named, tagging a 29,946 RTH high and a 30,001.5 overnight high before fading to close 29,807.25. The reclaim held into the close.
MES stays below the 7,777 stopTRIGGEREDFAILEDES did close under the old 7,777 line (7,766.5), but the downside continuation the row projected did not come. Instead of pressing toward the 7,739 low it reclaimed its own 7,761 trend stop and closed green (+0.17%), so the short-continuation thesis failed.
MGC stays below the 4,433 stop and loses the 4,387 RTH low on 2 hourly closesNOT TRIGGERED-Gold did the opposite. It rallied back above the 4,433 area, never went near the 4,387 low (session low 4,422.7), and closed 4,435.7 (+0.93%), repairing rather than extending the pullback.
MCL reclaims the 83.67 stop on 2 hourly closesTRIGGEREDPLAYED OUTThe reclaim branch did not fire; crude never got back above 83.67 (RTH high 83.46). The other branch did: it lost the 83.05 average on the close and cooled toward the 82.00 psych exactly as the row said, closing 82.59 with a 82.35 low.

Score: 5 rows, 3 triggered, 2 played out, 0 mixed, 1 failed, 2 not triggered. A risk-on reclaim day. The NQ reclaim scenario played out cleanly and crude's cool-off branch played out, while the ES short-continuation row failed as ES reclaimed its own stop and closed green. That is the first failed row of the month, and it happened because a benign CPI flipped the tape back up faster than the short thesis could work. Month to date (August): 40 rows, 27 triggered, 18 played out, 7 mixed, 1 failed.
